transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-05-01 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood SE), Lena (SkyVault Partnerships), Ravi (Cloud Arch), Aisha (VP Product), Tommy (Security)

Summary: quick partner intro, clarify integration modes (hosted vs dedicated vs private onramp), security posture, pilot scope and benchmarks, go/no-go criteria. Shared links: integration deck (https://redwood.app/partners/skyvault-integ-deck), pilot benchmark sheet (https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SKYVAULT-BENCH).

Topics: 1) Partnership goals and commercial model; 2) Technical integration patterns and APIs; 3) Security/compliance; 4) Pilot success criteria and benchmarks; 5) Next steps and owners.

00:00 - 00:32 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. This is Maya from Redwood inference, I'm the AE working with partners. Omar and Jules from our SE org are on to go deeper on infra. Quick round of intros?
00:33 - 01:05 Lena: Hi, I'm Lena, run partnerships at SkyVault Cloud, we do managed private cloud for regulated customers. Ravi runs infra, Tommy does security, and Aisha is our product lead for marketplace.
01:06 - 01:42 Maya: Great. Quick framing - we're looking to explore a tech onramp where Redwood would serve inference workloads either via a colocated dedicated pool on SkyVault or via an integration that routes customer requests to Redwood hosted but with tenancy controls. We're flexible. Wanted to understand constraints, success metrics, and security needs.
01:43 - 02:20 Ravi: Two big constraints for us: data residency and tenancy - many customers need their models to run in our VPC; also we have mixed GPU fleet (A100, H100, and some L4 for smaller embeddings). We care about predictable p95 lat and cost.
02:21 - 03:05 Omar: Understood. For predictable p95 we recommend dedicated capacity with reserved pools; we can also route lower-priority requests to hosted variants. Quick question: is SkyVault thinking to resell capacity or embed Redwood as a managed offering?
03:06 - 03:42 Aisha: Both are on the table. Primary goal is to offer low-friction inference for our enterprise customers. We want a partner model that allows revenue share, but also a private deployment option for customers that require it.
03:43 - 04:10 Jules: In terms of integration patterns we typically see three: 1) API-level redirect where your control plane calls our hosted API, 2) Dedicated pools deployed into partner cloud (we call Redwood Dedicated), and 3) Private deployment package where Redwood control plane is customer-managed. Each has different security/cost tradeoffs.
04:11 - 04:58 Tommy: For security: SOC2 is required by many of our customers; we also need SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, KMS/HSM for keys, and audit log forwarding into our SIEM. Can Redwood support forwarding logs and bring-your-own-key?
04:59 - 05:40 Omar: Yep — bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM is supported in our Private offering, and we can export audit logs; for hosted we have options for encrypted-in-transit and at-rest plus enterprise tenancy features. We'll share the security questionnaire.
05:41 - 06:30 Lena: Operational question — latency expectations. A lot of our customers are latency-sensitive (conversational agents). What numbers do you typically hit on H100 or A100?
06:31 - 07:20 Omar: Ballpark — for 8k context LLMs on H100 with optimized kernels, we see p50 around 40-70ms per token in batch-friendly scenarios, p95 depends on concurrency and KV cache patterns. We'll want to run an in-cloud benchmark to show realistic numbers on your fleet.
07:21 - 08:05 Ravi: That sounds reasonable but need to validate on our network topology. We also want to understand caching — will Redwood use KV cache across requests? Will that be shared across tenants?
08:06 - 09:02 Jules: We support KV cache and prefix caching; for multi-tenant setups we isolate KV per tenant. For dedicated pools deployed into your environment, caching is local to the pool to maximize hit rate. Sometimes transcribe shows it as 'K V cache' in our docs, sorry for the odd spacing.
09:03 - 11:00 Aisha: Commercially, we're evaluating revenue split vs seat licensing. We want a model where SkyVault can resell and mark up but still keep predictable margins for customers. Also is there an SLA we can guarantee?
11:01 - 12:05 Maya: We offer SLA-backed latency/uptime for Dedicated customers; hosted tiers have best-effort but enterprise tiers can be contract SA. For partner resell we'll work a tailored agreement. We'll loop in bizops after initial tech alignment.
12:06 - 14:00 Tommy: On compliance: some customers require on-prem or air-gapped deployment. Does Redwood have an offline/airgap package? Also need to confirm data retention and deletion options.
14:01 - 15:15 Omar: We do have a private deployment option suitable for regulated or air-gapped workflows; may need some engineering lead time for packaging. Deletion/retention controls are configurable and auditable. We'll send docs.
15:16 - 17:30 Ravi: Network egress: if you run a hosted control plane that needs to call our VMs, we have strict firewall rules. For pilot, what access will you need?
17:31 - 19:10 Jules: For a pilot we typically ask for a minimal set: ssh/API access to a staging GPU node, ingress rules for our test runner, a service account for pulling model artifacts, and log shipper access. We'll put a checklist in the pilot plan.
19:11 - 22:00 Lena: Timelinewise we have a marketplace roadmap aiming for beta in Q3. If pilot runs mid-May we could QA and target Q3 for general availability. What leads time do you need?
22:01 - 23:20 Maya: For a basic pilot we can do 4-6 weeks if infra access and security review move quickly. For Private/on-prem packaging that might be longer. We'll aim to start planning week of May 11.
23:21 - 28:00 Discussion (technical) - Omar dives into model packaging and quantization: we recommended quantizing to int8 for LLM inference where acceptable, and Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles. Some customers trade slight quality for 2-3x cost reduction. Mention of 'Redwood Optimise' mis-spelled in notes.
28:01 - 33:00 Ravi: We have concerns about kernel compatibility on older nodes (A100 gen1). How do you select kernels and fallback if perf regresses?
33:01 - 36:00 Omar: We have a kernel selection layer and a serving runtime that monitors per-model perf. We can pin kernel sets per rollout, and use automatic fallback to compatible variants. For older hardware we may recommend different batch sizes or model quantization. We'll share a perf profile example.
36:01 - 40:00 Aisha: Can we surface pricing transparency to our customers? Ideally per-token/unit pricing with per-route cost breakdown in the console.
40:01 - 43:00 Maya: Redwood Console shows token-level cost, per-route breakdowns, and can export. For reseller flows we can hide cost details or surface aggregated billing via our billing API.
43:01 - 49:00 Tommy: Security quick follow — we need to verify key custody options and whether HSM integration requires special hardware in our region. Also audit log retention requirements vary by customer.
49:01 - 52:00 Omar: HSM integration typically uses your cloud KMS; we have docs for AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault and can integrate with self-hosted HSMs. We'll attach the architecture note.
52:01 - 57:00 Action recap and pilot framing — Maya summarizes pilot goals: prove latency targets on SkyVault A100/H100 nodes, validate tenancy and KMS flows, run safety/regression evals on a handful of prompts, and test integration for audit log forwarding.
57:01 - 59:30 Lena: Sounds good. A couple of asks — can you provide a short list of minimum infra specs and an initial SOC2 artifact bundle? Also an NDA for marketplace commercial discussions?
59:31 - 61:50 Maya: We'll send scope doc, bench template, SOC2 link, and a partner NDA. Action owners: Maya/Omar to send docs; Ravi/Tommy to share infra inventory + answers.
61:51 - 62:00 Close: thanks and agreed to reconvene after docs exchanged.

Meeting highlights/notes (auto): - Positive fit: SkyVault seeks a managed onramp and reseller model. - Pilot focus: latency benchmarks on your GPU fleet, tenancy isolation (VPC/dedicated pools), KMS/HSM + audit logs. - Risk: packaging time for air-gapped on-prem option and kernel compatibility with older A100 nodes. - Commercial: revenue share model to be explored; need NDA and bizops follow-up.

Links referenced: Integration deck (https://redwood.app/partners/skyvault-integ-deck), Pilot bench sheet (https://drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SKYVAULT-BENCH), Security questionnaire (https://redwood.app/security/questionnaire).

End transcript.
